We have target molecule SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO

We have precursors from previous step: three possible pairs (product SMILES, Cl[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C). Those are likely the result of applying a template that does a silyl protection removal? Actually the product SMILES are the same as target? Wait target is same as first element of each pair? The list shows product SMILES (the same as target) and a silyl chloride reagent. So the template likely is a silyl deprotection? Actually the reaction is a silyl ether formation? The target contains O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C (a t-butyldimethylsilyl? Actually O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C is a TBDMS? That's t-butyldimethylsilyl: Si with two methyls and t-butyl. So the reaction could be silylation of an alcohol using Cl[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C (TBDMSCl). So the template is a protection step: alcohol + TBDMSCl -> silyl ether. In retrosynthesis, we would break that to give the alcohol and the silyl chloride.

Thus the template likely corresponds to a silyl protection reaction. The functional groups formed: "trimethylsilyl"? Actually functional group list includes "trimethylsilyl" and "t-butyldimethylsilyl". The target has t-butyldimethylsilyl ether. So functional group formed is "t-butyldimethylsilyl". Broken: "aliphatic hydroxyls" (the OH). So we can search with functional_groups_formed = ["t-butyldimethylsilyl"] and functional_groups_broken = ["aliphatic hydroxyls"].

Let's search.
